items.title: JPEG vs JPG: Is There Any Difference?
items.author: AFMEI
items.summary:
No. JPEG and JPG are the same image format. The only difference is the file extension: .jpeg has four letters and .jpg has three. Open the two files side by side and the picture data inside is built the same way.

If that's all you wanted to know, you're done. If you'd like to understand why two spellings exist, and when the extension can still cause trouble, keep reading.
